title.narrative: Enablers to Sustainable Trade and Investment in Africa

description.narrative: SummaryThis Action is central to the Global Gateway (GG) Africa-Europe Investment Package (GG AEIP) roll-out and contributes to the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) in support to African economic integration towards the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), a flagship objective of the African Union¿s Agenda 2063 and a major priority for the European Union (EU). The EU has built a strategic approach in support of intra-African and EU-Africa investment and trade by anchoring its support on key priority areas (i.e. trade in goods, services, trade facilitation, competition, digital trade) of free trade and investment agreements at continental, regional and national levels (AfCFTA, RECs, EU Bilateral and Regional - EPAs), as well as key value chains, and trade corridors.To complement this support, this Action will focus on four additional key enablers of EU-Africa and intra-Africa sustainable trade and investment that will be concretely implemented through four different projects, some of which are a continuation of existing support, namely:1. Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) protection and enforcement are key for investment and innovation facilitation and protection. Support will contribute to the harmonisation, creation, registration, management, utilisation and administration, protection, and enforcement of IPRs in Africa. To this end, the Action will focus on continental, regional and national: (i) African IP legal and policy frameworks (i.e. AfCFTA IP Protocol, the Continental Strategy for Geographical Indications (GIs) of the African Union, Regional and national IP regulations, etc.); (ii) African IP administration capacities; (iii) African and EU productive sector support, with a particular focus on SMEs (i.e. the Africa IP SME Helpdesk); and (iv) Support to the elaboration and implementation of the post 2023 Continental Strategy for GIs of the African Union.2. EU-Africa Trade and Investment Agreements, with the main objective to boost sustainable EU ¿ Africa trade and investment flows and strengthen the trade and investment capacities of African partners through the design of a flexible on-demand facility that can offer ad-hoc support to countries with whom the EU has concluded trade and investment agreements (EPAs, SIFAs, etc.). This facility will also provide complementary technical support needed for alignment with EU regulations and directives having an impact on EU-Africa trade and investment, such as the relevant policies adopted in the framework of the European Green Deal and the EU Circular Economy Action Plan or the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CS3D).3. Customs Cooperation, a main enabler at the basis of all trade. The Action proposes a follow up to the existing successful programmes `Harmonizing the classification of goods based on WCO standards to enhance African trade¿ (EU-WCO Harmonised System (HS) Programme, 2018-2024) and `Implementation and application of Rules of Origin (RoO)¿ (EU-WCO RoO Programme, 2021-2025). The scope of the new programme is to enhance African trade by further developing and implementing key customs pillars of the AfCFTA and of other regional agreements through dedicated technical capacity support to (i) Harmonised System (HS), (ii) Rules of Origin (RoO), and (iii) Valuation. 4. Investment Facilitation, a crucial soft enabler to accompany Global Gateway hard investments, ensuring that they are conducive to sustainable and inclusive development.
